findings.location: J1 pins 1 and 2 in the saved schematic and PCB
findings.mechanism: The saved circuit connects J1.1 to R1.1 (/IN), while J1.2 connects to R1.2 and C1.1 (/OUT). C1 therefore shunts the contracted input rather than the filtered output. J1.3 correctly connects to ground.
findings.reasoning: This is a saved topology mismatch, not merely reversed net names. With V1 and V2 measured relative to J1.3 and arbitrary output admittance Yload(s), output-node KCL gives V1/V2 = 1/(1 + R1·Yload(s)); C1 supplies no output-side RC pole in that relation. Actual source-to-output response depends on unspecified external impedances, but the reversed connector mapping is directly established. Clean schematic parity confirms that both native files share the mismatch.
findings.title: J1 input and filtered-output connections are reversed

limitations: No physical measurements or simulation; no supplied behavioral models, stimuli or measurements to validate.
Source/load-dependent response, voltage/current/thermal limits, tolerances and parasitics were not evaluated because operating conditions and component ratings were unspecified.
ERC/DRC were reviewed from supplied fresh records, not rerun; ignored rule categories remain unchecked. Zone fill was assessed as saved without refill.

Detailed manufacturing and mechanical qualification were not independently audited. Active reset and brownout behavior is inapplicable to this passive network; source-dependent startup/shutdown response was not evaluated.
